# Independent Adobe import sources

The 16 `.aep` files in this directory were authored in Adobe After Effects,
not generated by the FX writer. Their `.ae.json` sidecars pin the native source
hash, byte count, composition/layer identity, Adobe version and authored controls.
`structure_document/tests/native_sources.rs` contains 16 fresh-import editable
structure assertions against them. The two Rectangle/Fill assertions target
main's native editable `Rect` representation, not the former generated path.

The historical `export_*` names are retained to preserve native identity and
provenance; these files are now inputs to import tests, not writer outputs or
claims about export support. Sidecar `reference_*` fields describe the historical
24fps local renders, not the current expected-video corpus or published Assets.
Those 11 legacy files remain local only; every current expected is generated
fresh at **30fps in Adobe**, including replacements for those cases.

The authoritative [AE expected-video manifest](../aep_video_references.json)
tracks all 415 compositions in the 62 source AEPs. Native source FPS stays 24;
Adobe's render setting `Use this frame rate: 30` changes output sampling without
editing the source. `-s`/`-e` use native source-frame indices, so a two-second
24fps source uses `-s 0 -e 47` and produces 60 output frames. Dimensions and full
composition duration are preserved.

Expected video binaries must not be committed or pushed to GitHub. Rendered
files and contact sheets live in ignored `.expected-30fps/` storage. Videos are
published as **long-term Assets**; the manifest records Asset IDs, source and
composition identity, content hashes, dimensions, duration and output FPS.
`verified` means Adobe output passed metadata/full-decode checks and a freshly
resolved download matched the uploaded bytes/SHA. Pending or blocked entries
are not completed uploads. Visual inspection is recorded separately.

Publication is complete: **415/415** references, 415 distinct long-term Asset
IDs, 34,590 output frames, 44,693,811 video bytes. All 415 local MP4 hashes match
the manifest and all 62 original AEP hashes remain unchanged. Every reference
was freshly retrieved and hash-verified during publication.

Content inspection is not a feature-adequacy verdict. In particular, sampled
`MEDIA_REPLACED_INSTANCE` and `MEDIA_SOURCE` both show blue footage, and
`CLOCK_REVERSE_BEZIER` samples are black. Some miter/trim/selector samples do
not visibly distinguish parameter changes. Closed-rectangle cap cases are not
cap proof; separate open-line `CAP_*` cases also exist. Per-composition
observations and limitations are recorded in the manifest. Do not treat these
publication records as 415 passing feature tests.

No automated AEP/FX render comparison gate is enrolled. A verified publication is not
an import/render-fidelity pass. RGB MP4s do not establish alpha or audio fidelity.

Obsolete edited-FX inputs, writer readbacks, comparison reports and proof-runner
code are intentionally excluded. Sidecar `edited_fx_*` fields and old writer
support claims have been removed. `author_jsx*_sha256` and render-log hashes are
historical provenance; they do not imply those scripts/logs are packaged here.
The original provenance is recoverable in PR #4415's pre-cleanup commit
`33c9bee22d6b041d79089335280a4592b2975b9a`.

The branch was rebased onto main's landed implementation (#4422). Retaining the
assertions does not establish that they pass against that version. Subsequent
Adobe-native expected generation/publication is separate from importer execution
or AEP/FX render comparison. No product code or export behavior is changed by these fixtures.

See [the grouped source map](../import_sources.md) for the separate 46-file
collection and its remaining proof/portability limitations.
